title: Object of saving faith: all revealed things — principally the Gospel promises
source_text: XX. Sed ut planius & manifestius fiat quid Reformati sentiant de fidei justificantis natura atque essentia, paucis exponenda sunt ea quae docent de ejus objecto, partibus, & actibus. Primum ergo quod spectat fidei salvificae & justificantis objectum, ad illud communiter pertinere affirmant omnia illa quae Deus in verbo suo revelavit. Nec enim quicquam eorum fides illa non suscipit, quum ipsi proponuntur, sed tamen proprium ejus & praecipuum objectum esse censent Evangelii promissiones, quibus misericordia & gratia Dei per Christum offertur omnibus vere credentibus & resipiscentibus.
pass_a_gloss: But that it may become plainer and more manifest what the Reformed think concerning the nature and essence of justifying faith, those things are to be briefly set forth which they teach concerning its object, parts, and acts. First therefore as regards the object of saving and justifying faith, they affirm that all those things which God has revealed in His word commonly pertain to it. For that faith does not refuse any of them when they are proposed to it; yet they judge its proper and principal object to be the promises of the Gospel, by which the mercy and grace of God through Christ are offered to all who truly believe and repent.
pass_b_english: Next: object, parts, and acts of justifying faith.
Object commonly: all God revealed in His word — faith refuses none when proposed.
Proper and principal object: Gospel promises.
Mercy and grace through Christ offered to all who truly believe and repent.
